$comment: Runtime profiles are orthogonal to delivery modes. A mode decides WHO works on the code (agents and stages). A profile decides HOW the agent runs (portability vs. token cost). Switch with: devcrew profile <name>

normal.label: Normal — portable
normal.use: Cursor, Antigravity, VS Code, Copilot, Codex, or a team where not everyone installs extra tooling. Zero external dependencies.
normal.notes: Everything works with no install step. Token discipline is still enforced by hooks — budgets, delegation, on-demand reads — you just don't get the extra compression layers.

optimized.label: Optimized — minimum tokens
optimized.use: Claude Code, or any agent that supports skills and command hooks, when context and cost are the binding constraint.
optimized.notes: Adds three compression layers on top of the hooks: caveman on what the agent writes, rtk on what tool calls return, and a blocking DESIGN.md token lint so design values are never re-derived in prose. Installs third-party software — always an explicit choice, never the default.
